key_insight: Scaling automated discovery is not just about adding more agent time or more agents—it can require forgetting past history to keep making progress. The paper finds that as LLM research agents accumulate context, different scaling strategies eventually plateau.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the challenge of how to continue improving automated research agents when iterative search, parallel exploration, and agent collaboration all stop yielding new discoveries due to growing historical baggage.
method: Study three scaling strategies for LLM-based research agents: longer single-agent iteration, multiple agents in parallel, and communicating multi-agent systems.
Analyze how accumulated history affects discovery performance and identify when/why progress plateaus.
Motivate forgetting or resetting parts of agent memory/history as a mechanism to restore exploration and continued improvement.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests that bigger search budgets alone may not improve automated discovery. Designing agents with controlled forgetting, pruning, or reset mechanisms may be essential for sustained research performance.
visual_elements: A plateau curve showing performance vs. iteration count for the three scaling strategies.
A three-panel comparison diagram: single agent, parallel agents, communicating agents.
A memory/history buildup icon illustrating how accumulated context slows discovery.
A before/after schematic showing full-history agents versus agents that forget or prune old context.
paper_authors: Shangyin Tan, Ben Zhou, Lakshya A Agrawal, Jialin Zhang, Yilin Chen
